description: we are a young couple with backgrounds in Data Science and Medicine. we're very passionate about universe as well as video games
summary: We created Sol by Sol, a web-based game designed for children ages 7 to 12, in hopes of teaching them all about what life and survival would really be like on a Mars mission, in a fun way of course !
details:
Our project is quite straightforward. Its a survival game where the player is an astronaut on a 10 day mission on Mars, with the goal of surviving the harsh conditions of the planet and finding enough sulfur crystals to bring back to Earth, while taking care of their overall health. Our goal is to teach kids about complex subjects related to space travel such as microgravity, radiation exposure and the impact it can have on humans in an interactive and fun way. We avoided all use of scientific jargon and removed all units of measurement to avoid any confusion and to make it more kid-friendly.

What makes our game creative is that we used real NASA data and implemented it in the game mechanics. For instance, the solar flares and dust storms that take place in the game are all real events that were recorded by NASA's Curiosity rover. However, the weather forecast can sometimes be wrong, just like in real life. The location in which the game takes place is a real place on Mars called Gale crater, and the terrain topography is faithful to the MOLA height map. Player health is influenced by environmental factors of course, but we also found it important to incorporate the idea of mental health. If the player stays cooped up for too long inside the shelter or doesn't communicate with his family back home for too long, his/her health bar goes down. In terms of graphic design, we decided to go with a storybook theme, the base being a cozy glowing martian outpost at dusk. Moreover, rewards are real. Each crystal found unlocks a real photograph taken by Curiosity. We also stay transparent when it comes to science facts. In the game's menu, we have a page citing which parts of the game are real NASA data and which parts are game rules.

We used Claude AI to help us code the game, and built it using Three.js, WebAudio, Javascript, HTML, CSS, GLSL, Python Github, Microsoft neural text-to-speech, as well as all of the NASAs APIs mentioned below. We considered factors such as scientific accuracy, player understanding of said science, entertainment and replayability. We also made sure to make it accessible for all, on any device. You can therefore play it on the web via computer, tablet or mobile phone.
